name: Portugal
headline_status: Cannabis is not legal in Portugal, but possessing a personal-use amount has been decriminalised since 2001, and medical cannabis is sold in pharmacies.
summary: Portugal decriminalised possession of all drugs for personal use in 2001, treating amounts up to a 10-day supply (25 g of herbal cannabis or 5 g of hashish) as an administrative matter handled by dissuasion commissions. A 2023 law change stopped treating larger amounts as automatic proof of trafficking. Selling cannabis remains a crime. Medical cannabis was legalised in July 2018 and is dispensed through pharmacies.

possession_limit.value: Buying or holding drugs for one's own use is an administrative offence, not a crime. Holding more than the average 10-day supply (25 g of herbal cannabis or 5 g of hashish under Portaria 94/96) is only an indication that the purpose may not be personal use; since Law 55/2023, if personal use is shown the case is closed and referred to a dissuasion commission.

penalties.value: People found with drugs for personal use are referred to a Commission for the Dissuasion of Drug Addiction, which can refer them to treatment or impose administrative sanctions. Selling or distributing cannabis is a crime carrying prison time under Decree-Law 15/93.

public_use.value: Using cannabis, in public or in private, is an administrative offence (contraordenação) handled by the dissuasion commissions rather than the courts; there is no place where recreational use is legal.

retail_sales.value: None. There is no legal framework for recreational sales, and selling cannabis is a crime under Decree-Law 15/93.

medical_since.value: July 2018: Law No. 33/2018 of 18 July set the framework for medicines, preparations and substances based on the cannabis plant, dispensed in pharmacies on prescription.

home_grow.value: Not allowed. Growing cannabis for one's own use is a crime punishable by up to 3 months in prison or a fine of up to 30 days, although the court may waive the penalty.

tourists.value: Visitors are treated like residents: personal use and possession are administrative offences referred to a dissuasion commission, and there is no legal place to buy.

timeline.event: Law No. 30/2000 takes effect, making use and possession of all drugs for personal use an administrative offence
Law No. 33/2018 sets the legal framework for medical cannabis dispensed through pharmacies
Law No. 55/2023 takes effect: amounts above a 10-day supply are only an indication, not proof, of trafficking

faq.a: No, but possessing up to 25 g of cannabis (a 10-day supply) is decriminalised and handled as an administrative matter rather than a crime.

faq.q: Can tourists smoke weed in Portugal?
faq.a: Visitors are treated like residents: small amounts are not a crime, but public use can be fined and there is no legal way to buy.

faq.q: Is medical cannabis legal in Portugal?
faq.a: Yes. Medical cannabis was legalised in 2018 and is dispensed by pharmacies with a prescription.
